earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 ex991_q326.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 October 20, 2026 Fellow shareholders, • We delivered our Q3 forecast and expect to deliver on our full year 2026 guidance. ◦ Q3 revenue grew 12% year over year (11% on a F/X neutral basis 1 ) to $12.9B, consistent with our forecast. Operating margin was 34.6%, up from 28.2% in Q3’25 and ahead of our forecast primarily due to the timing of expenses. ◦ For 2026, we expect revenue of $51.1B (+13% year over year) and an operating margin of 31.5%. • The core of our service is delivering differentiated, exclusive, professionally produced series, films and live events. Q3 highlights include The Last House , Facing El Chapo , Death of the Pastor’s Wife , our NFL Game from Melbourne, and a very successful slate in India. • We’ll continue to expand our entertainment offering through licensing and new ways to bring more third-party content to our service, like our TF1 partnership in France. Our audience, which is approaching one billion people, and our best-in-class product capabilities, make us great partners for studios, networks and creative talent. • Member response to our 2026 price changes is consistent with prior adjustments and our expectations, an indicator that our engagement - which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing - remains healthy and that we continue to deliver strong value to members. • We’ll close out 2026 with an exciting slate including The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , limited series The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey , starring Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen, new seasons of The Diplomat , Nobody Wants This and Lupin , the series finale of Emily in Paris , three NFL games on Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas Day, and the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua fight. Our summary results, and forecast for Q4, are below. (in millions except per share data) Q3'25 Q4'25 Q1'26 Q2'26 Q3'26 Q4'26 Forecast Revenue $ 11,510 $ 12,051 $ 12,250 $ 12,560 $ 12,874 $ 13,442 Y/Y % Growth 17.2 % 17.6 % 16.2 % 13.4 % 11.8 % 11.5 % Operating Income $ 3,248 $ 2,957 $ 3,957 $ 4,193 $ 4,459 $ 3,500 Operating Margin 28.2 % 24.5 % 32.3 % 33.4 % 34.6 % 26.0 % Net Income $ 2,547 $ 2,419 $ 5,283 $ 3,401 $ 3,664 $ 2,787 Diluted EPS $ 0.59 $ 0.56 $ 1.23 $ 0.80 $ 0.87 $ 0.67 Net cash provided by operating activities $ 2,825 $ 2,112 $ 5,290 $ 1,744 $ 3,162 Free Cash Flow $ 2,660 $ 1,872 $ 5,094 $ 1,525 $ 2,884 Shares (FD) 4,340 4,317 4,298 4,261 4,195 __________________________________ 1 Excluding the year over year effect of foreign exchange rate movements and the impact of hedging gains/losses realized as revenues. Assumes foreign exchange rates remained constant with foreign exchange rates from each of the corresponding months of the prior-year period. 1 Q3 Results and Forecast Revenue in Q3 grew 12% year over year (+11% on a foreign exchange (F/X) neutral basis), and was in-line with our forecast. In Q3, revenue growth was driven primarily by subscription revenue, reflecting increases in memberships and pricing, growth in advertising revenue and a favorable impact from F/X rates, net of hedging. Membership growth benefited from continued, healthy retention in every region; globally and in the US, churn improved year-over-year and was better than forecast. Q3’26 operating income totaled $4.5B (+37% year over year) and operating margin of 34.6% was up versus 28.2% in Q3’25. Both Q3 operating income and margin were ahead of forecast due primarily to the timing of expenses and the slight upside in revenue. As a result, diluted EPS for the quarter amounted to $0.87 vs. $0.59 in Q3’25 (+49% year over year). As a reminder, the guidance we provide is our actual internal forecast at the time we report and we strive for accuracy. Our primary financial metrics are revenue for growth and operating margin for profitability. Our goal is to sustain healthy revenue growth, expand operating profit and margin, and deliver growing free cash flow. In Q4, we expect revenue of $13.4 billion, which represents year over year growth of 12% (or 11% F/X neutral) driven by growth in memberships, pricing, and ad revenue. We project a Q4 operating margin of 26.0% which includes ~120 basis points negative impact associated with our recently announced headcount reductions, and compares with 24.5% in the year ago quarter. These organizational changes enable us to continue to aggressively invest in high impact areas to improve our service, and drive growth and innovation. Our guidance for Q4 means that for the full year 2026 we expect revenue of $51.1B, or growth of 13% (+12% on a F/X neutral basis). This is 0.2% below the mid-point of our prior 2026 revenue forecast range - while subscription revenue growth has outperformed our expectations, we currently expect 2026 ad revenue of ~$2.7B vs. approximately $3B previously (due to slightly slower than expected rollout of some ad product capabilities). We anticipate an operating margin of 31.5% for 2026 (31.4% based on F/X rates as of January 1, 2026) vs. 29.5% in 2025. Our updated 2026 margin guidance includes ~30 basis points negative impact associated with our Q4 headcount reductions. Our forecast implies annual operating income growth of 20%+ for 2026. Our Focus Our mission is to entertain the world while building a wildly successful business. Our strategy is simple: invest in differentiated, exclusive, professionally-produced entertainment like Netflix originals that spark conversation, bring in more members, and make us a “must-have” service. We pair these originals, which anchor our service, with a broad, complementary selection of third-party programming, a great discovery experience, and leading global distribution. Together, this fuels engagement (quality, quantity, and variety of viewing) and, in turn, revenue and profit. The core of our service is streaming TV, film and live events, monetized via subscription and advertising. It represents the vast majority of our spending and nearly all of our revenue, and is the engine of our business for which we see a long runway of growth. To successfully execute this strategy, we focus on three priorities: 1) delivering more entertainment value to our members, 2) leveraging technology to improve all aspects of our service, and 3) improving our monetization. These priorities work in concert to drive acquisition and retention, create member value that lets us occasionally raise prices, and increase advertiser demand. We reinvest returns in our business so we can win more moments of truth and fund the next wave of entertainment. Done well, 2 this makes our service the one where members go first to look for entertainment and the last service they would cancel, with industry-leading retention and continued member and ARM 2 growth. With intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention, strategic clarity and excellent execution are critical. In Q3, we delivered well across all three priorities, but we see room to do even better with focused, continuous improvement. In Q3, we had a variety of hits from around the world that members loved. Plastic Beauty * (12M views 3 ) is on track to be our most-viewed series ever in Japan; The Secret Woman * (47M) is trending to be our most-viewed Danish title ever; Facing El Chapo * (58M) is pacing to be our second most-viewed Mexican title globally; and The Perfect Lie * (17M) is on track to become our most-viewed series out of the Netherlands. Non-English viewing has grown from under 10% of total viewing a decade ago to more than a third today. These hits reflect our decade-long commitment to creating content around the world that resonates locally, and has the potential to travel globally. Other successful Q3 titles include: • UCAN : Death of the Pastor's Wife* (45M), The Idaho Murders: College Nightmare* (38M), My Life With The Walter Boys S3* (29M), Little House on the Prairie (29M), The Last House* (91M) and Why Did I Get Married Again* (36M) • EMEA : The Gentlemen S2* (33M) and A Toxic Love Story* (43M) from the UK, Elite Force* (25M) from France, Blood Sacrifice* (23M) from Sweden • LATAM : My Daughter's Father* (23M) from Mexico and Nando Between Two Worlds - A Sintonia Film * (18M) from Brazil • APAC : The East Palace (21M) and Our Sticky Love* (22M) from Korea Complementing our Netflix originals, we continue to expand our entertainment offering through licensing and bringing more third-party content to our service in new ways. Our broad distribution (we’re serving an audience approaching one billion people) and industry leading monetization make us great partners for studios, networks and creative talent. For example, we partnered with Take-Two to unveil a sneak peek of the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI 5 in August. And we recently secured a new licensing deal with Disney 6 which brings a variety of current and library series and films to our service for our members to enjoy, including all five Ice Age films which reached our global weekly Top 10 list and are building consumer awareness in advance of Disney’s theatrical release of Ice Age: Boiling Point in February 2027. __________________________________ 2 Average revenue per membership. 3 A view is defined as hours viewed divided by runtime for each title. Views for a title are based on the first 91 days since the release of each episode (less than 91 days denoted with an asterisk and data is from launch date through October 18, 2026). We publish our top titles based on views each week at Netflix Top 10 4 . 4 https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10 5 https://www.ign.com/articles/gta-6-just-blew-me-away-im-so-glad-i-avoided-the-leaks 6 https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/disney-licenses-titles-netflix-ice-age-movies-will-trent-percy-jackson-and-the-olympians-felicity-1236897256/ 3 Our investment in our product capabilities, including our new TV UI, enables us to seamlessly integrate and merchandise more third party content to Netflix members. This summer we launched our partnership with TF1, a leading French broadcaster. This partnership enables us to provide our French members with even more highly local series, film, news and sports programming, all within a frictionless choosing and viewing experience that complements our French slate and global programming. We’re pleased with the TF1 partnership and the early metrics indicate that it’s generating incremental viewing in France. We also continue to invest in our ad tech stack (Netflix Ads Suite). In Q3, we extended programmatic access through globally-available CTV marketplace deals, and secured new partnerships with MercadoLibre in LATAM and AdForm in EMEA. We are also expanding capabilities to in-DSP measurement including reach, frequency, and attribution. Also, we will introduce our advertising tier to 15 new countries in 2027. The first tranche of new market launches will happen in March 2027: nine countries in EMEA 7 , Colombia, Peru and New Zealand (a new addition from our previous announcement). We know there’s some investor concern about our view hours growth. Member response to our 2026 price increases is consistent with prior price changes and our expectations, an indicator that our engagement - which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing - remains healthy and that we continue to deliver strong value to members. But we do seek to accelerate growth in view hours as well, and we’re confident we’ll do that by relentlessly focusing and executing against the aforementioned strategy. __________________________________ 7 https://about.netflix.com/en/news/netflix-hosts-first-uk-upfront 4 That confidence comes from seeing strong results when we execute well on our core strategy – our business in India in Q3 is an example. We delivered a great slate led by Lock Upp , our first daily reality series, which drove the most viewing of any title on Netflix in India ever 8 , the new scripted series Musafir Cafe * (9M) and the hit series Operation Safed Sagar * (11M). reference.summary: Netflix, Inc. provides entertainment services worldwide. The company offers television (TV) series, documentaries, feature films, games, and live programming across various genres and languages. It also provides members the ability to receive streaming content through a host of internet-connected devices, including TVs, digital video players, TV set-top boxes, and mobile devices. Netflix, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.
